pr_title: commands: introduce non_desktop command for output
pr_body:
This command allows users to set a given output as non-desktop. The output is offered to the drm-lease-manager interface if available, for clients to lease.

Closes #7021
pr_comments:
I'd prefer to name this something else. "non desktop" is just a hint coming from the kernel. This command allows one to lease "desktop" outputs.

tl;dr something like "drm_lease" would be a better name IMHO.

Now that you're saying it out loud it does make a lot of sense to have a `lease` command instead of using `non_desktop`. But that changes the scope of the whole patchset. 

Should true non-desktop output still be treated differently? Or should we treat them as regular output and already lease them unless the users requests to withdraw them?

issue_context.title: Create some way of dynamically setting displays as desktop or non-desktop
issue_context.body:
Two use-cases:
* I have a display that says it's non-desktop (like say an Index) and for some reason I want to extend the desktop to it anyway
* I have a display that looks to Sway like a normal monitor (like say a Project North Star AR headset) and I need to tell Sway to treat it as non-desktop so that Monado can do direct mode with it

This mostly was generated by discussion in Monado's IRC channel, let me know if you need more detail
comments:
> for some reason I want to extend the desktop to it anyway

What is this reason?

> I have a display that looks to Sway like a normal monitor (like say a Project North Star AR headset) and I need to tell Sway to treat it as non-desktop so that Monado can do direct mode with it

It would be better to send a kernel patch for this, so that everyone benefits from it without having to manually configure their compositor.

> Why would I want to extend the desktop to it anyway

* I work on Monado, and I break things all the time. In general, when direct mode is broken, it's useful to see if the compositor can extend. 

* If, god forbid, if you're trying to use SteamVR for Linux under Wayland, extended mode *might* work, but direct mode definitely wouldn't.

* Some VR headsets (I think PSVR is one? *Maybe* NReal Air?) have a "cinema mode" where it will correctly undistort the input signal so you can use it like a regular 2D monitor without any extra work. In this case, either cinema mode won't work or direct mode won't work, unless there's some way to dynamically tell the compositor what to do

* Even without cinema mode, you can (and I have) used HMDs as very janky monitors. Highly not recommended, but you can do it.

> It would be better to send a kernel patch for this

Yeah, but that's really annoying if you're hacking on XR display hardware and have a prototype display that nobody else is going to use and for which patches wouldn't be accepted. Or, maybe you want to set a very normal monitor to non-desktop for demos or debugging. We should probably try to make a kernel patch for North Star, but that's beside the point here.

In general, this feature request is indeed more of a developer tool - most "regular" setups will work well with Sway's default behaviour! This is mainly for XR developers who need to do crazy things

Also, FWIW, this feature request is directly analogous to X's `xrandr --output <OUTPUT> --prop --set non-desktop {0,1}`. The main thing I'm asking for is a copy of that behaviour, nothing more

Also also, I'm pretty okay at C/C++ - if you think this fits architecturally, you could give me an overview of what needs to be changed and I'd be happy to do it myself. I have plenty of hardware to test with :)
@emersion I think it would be easier to handle that in sway with the IPC to let user offer/withdraw outputs on the fly

review_comments: Hmm. Do we really need to do this? I don't like writing to the `wlr_output` struct.
I don't recally why I did that, maybe a leftover from a previous draft. I'll remove it.

We already have a function to do this:

```
struct sway_output *sway_output = all_output_by_name_or_id(oc->name);
```

It also handles output identifiers.
`all_output_by_name_or_id` searches in `root->all_outputs`,  is it better? I didnt get the difference between the two lists.
Maybe fail early in this case?
